title: ICSE CLASS 10 — Chemistry | Modern Periodic Table
description: Subject-wise test on Modern Periodic Table (Chemistry) for ICSE CLASS 10. 25Q.
subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct Modern Periodic Law?

options.text: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses
options.explanation: This was the basis of the older Mendeleev's periodic table, not the Modern Periodic Law.

options.text: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers
options.explanation: This is the correct statement of the Modern Periodic Law.

options.text: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their neutron numbers
options.explanation: Neutron numbers do not determine the periodic properties of elements.

options.text: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their valency
options.explanation: Valency is a derived property and does not govern the periodicity of elements.

questions.explanation: Modern Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers, as proposed by Moseley.
questions.hint: Focus on the key term 'Modern Periodic Law' and its defining feature.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: In the Modern Periodic Table, the element with atomic number 19 belongs to which period?

options.text: Period 2
options.explanation: Period 2 consists of elements with atomic numbers 3 to 10.

options.text: Period 3
options.explanation: Period 3 consists of elements with atomic numbers 11 to 18.

options.text: Period 4
options.explanation: Potassium (K) has an atomic number of 19 and is placed in Period 4.

options.text: Period 5
options.explanation: Period 5 consists of elements with atomic numbers 19 to 36, but Potassium is specifically in Period 4.

questions.explanation: The element with atomic number 19 is Potassium (K), which is placed in Period 4 of the Modern Periodic Table.
questions.hint: Recall that periods in the periodic table are determined by the number of electron shells.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the trend of atomic size in the Modern Periodic Table?

options.text: Atomic size increases down a group and decreases across a period
options.explanation: This is the correct trend observed in the periodic table.

options.text: Atomic size decreases down a group and increases across a period
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the actual trend.

options.text: Atomic size remains constant down a group and increases across a period
options.explanation: Atomic size does not remain constant down a group.

options.text: Atomic size increases down a group and remains constant across a period
options.explanation: Atomic size decreases across a period due to increased nuclear charge.

questions.explanation: Atomic size increases down a group due to the addition of new shells and decreases across a period due to the increase in nuclear charge pulling electrons closer.
questions.hint: Consider the factors affecting atomic size: number of electron shells and nuclear charge.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): The first ionization energy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen. Reason (R): Nitrogen has a half-filled p-subshell, which is more stable.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The assertion and reason are both correct, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason is also true.

questions.explanation: Nitrogen has a higher first ionization energy due to its half-filled p-subshell, which is more stable. Hence, both assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.
questions.hint: Analyze the electronic configurations of nitrogen and oxygen to understand their ionization energies.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?

options.text: Chlorine
options.explanation: Chlorine has a high electronegativity but not the highest.

options.text: Fluorine
options.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

options.text: Oxygen
options.explanation: Oxygen has a high electronegativity but not the highest.

options.text: Nitrogen
options.explanation: Nitrogen has a moderate electronegativity compared to fluorine.

questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity value of 3.98 on the Pauling scale due to its small atomic size and high nuclear charge.
questions.hint: Fluorine is known to be the most electronegative element on the periodic table.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which block does the element with atomic number 26 belong to?

options.text: s-block
options.explanation: The s-block includes elements where the last electron enters the s-orbital.

options.text: p-block
options.explanation: The p-block includes elements where the last electron enters the p-orbital.

options.text: d-block
options.explanation: Iron (Fe) has its last electron in the d-orbital, placing it in the d-block.

options.text: f-block
options.explanation: The f-block includes elements where the last electron enters the f-orbital.

questions.hint: The block of an element is determined by the subshell that receives the last electron during its filling.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of elements shows a reversal in the expected trend of atomic size?

options.text: Na and Mg
options.explanation: Sodium and Magnesium follow the expected trend of increasing atomic size down a group.

options.text: Be and B
options.explanation: Beryllium and Boron follow the expected trend of decreasing atomic size across a period.

options.text: Al and Ga
options.explanation: Gallium (Ga) is larger than Aluminum (Al) due to the poor shielding effect of d-electrons.

options.text: Li and Na
options.explanation: Lithium and Sodium follow the expected trend of increasing atomic size down a group.

questions.explanation: Gallium (Ga) has a larger atomic size than Aluminum (Al) due to the poor shielding effect of the d-electrons in Ga, causing an increase in atomic size.
questions.hint: Consider the presence of d-electrons and their shielding effect on the atomic size.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: The element with atomic number 17 is placed in which group of the Modern Periodic Table?

options.text: Group 1
options.explanation: Group 1 contains alkali metals.

options.text: Group 15
options.explanation: Group 15 contains nitrogen group elements.

options.text: Group 17
options.explanation: Chlorine (Cl) belongs to Group 17 (Halogens).

options.text: Group 18
options.explanation: Group 18 contains noble gases.

questions.explanation: The element with atomic number 17 is Chlorine (Cl), which belongs to Group 17 (Halogens) in the Modern Periodic Table.
questions.hint: Recall the groups in the periodic table and the elements they contain.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect about noble gases?

options.text: They are placed in Group 18 of the Modern Periodic Table
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: They have very low ionization energies
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect; noble gases have very high ionization energies.

options.text: They are chemically inert under normal conditions
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: They have completely filled s and p orbitals in their valence shell
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

questions.explanation: Noble gases have very high ionization energies due to their stable electronic configurations, not low ionization energies.
questions.hint: Consider the properties of noble gases and their electronic configurations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of the element with atomic number 35?

options.text: It forms salts with metals
options.explanation: This is a property of halogens.

options.text: It is a liquid at room temperature
options.explanation: Bromine is a liquid at room temperature, but the question asks for a property that is NOT true.

options.text: It has seven electrons in its valence shell
options.explanation: This is a property of halogens.

options.text: It is highly reactive
options.explanation: This is a property of halogens.

questions.explanation: Bromine (atomic number 35) is a liquid at room temperature, whereas other halogens like fluorine, chlorine, and iodine are gases or solids. Hence, option B is incorrect.
questions.hint: Recall the physical state of halogens at room temperature.

options.text: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers
options.explanation: This is the correct statement of the Modern Periodic Law.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the trend of atomic radii in the Modern Periodic Table?

options.text: Increases down a group and decreases across a period
options.explanation: This correctly describes the trend of atomic radii in the periodic table.

options.text: Decreases down a group and increases across a period
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct trend.

options.text: Increases down a group and increases across a period
options.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period, not increases.

options.text: Decreases down a group and decreases across a period
options.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group, not decreases.

questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group due to the addition of new electron shells, and decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge which pulls electrons closer to the nucleus.
questions.hint: Consider how the number of electron shells and nuclear charge affect atomic size.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The first ionization energy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen. Reason (R): Nitrogen has a half-filled p-orbital which is more stable.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both statements are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true
options.explanation: The assertion A is true.

questions.explanation: The first ionization energy of nitrogen (7) is higher than that of oxygen (8) because nitrogen has a half-filled p-orbital (stable configuration), making it harder to remove an electron. Hence, both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
questions.hint: Analyze the electronic configurations of nitrogen and oxygen to understand their ionization energies.

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?

options.text: Sodium
options.explanation: Sodium is a highly reactive alkali metal with low electronegativity.

options.text: Magnesium
options.explanation: Magnesium has a higher electronegativity than sodium but lower than fluorine.

options.text: Chlorine
options.explanation: Chlorine has high electronegativity but is less than fluorine.

options.text: Fluorine
options.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among all elements.

questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group. Fluorine (F), being at the top right of the periodic table (excluding noble gases), has the highest electronegativity value of 3.98 on the Pauling scale.
questions.hint: Look for the element located at the top right of the periodic table (excluding noble gases).

questions.question: The element with atomic number 35 belongs to which group and period in the Modern Periodic Table?

options.text: Group 15, Period 4
options.explanation: Group 15 elements have five valence electrons, not seven.

options.text: Group 16, Period 3
options.explanation: Group 16 elements have six valence electrons and period 3 elements have three electron shells.

options.text: Group 17, Period 4
options.explanation: Bromine has seven valence electrons and four electron shells, placing it in Group 17 and Period 4.

options.text: Group 18, Period 3
options.explanation: Group 18 elements are noble gases with full valence shells.

questions.explanation: Atomic number 35 corresponds to Bromine (Br). Bromine is in Group 17 (halogens) and Period 4, as it has four electron shells and seven valence electrons.
questions.hint: Write the electronic configuration of the element with atomic number 35 to determine its group and period.

questions.question: The student notes that the ionization energy does not increase uniformly. Which statement best explains the anomaly between magnesium (Mg) and aluminum (Al)?

options.text: Magnesium has a higher nuclear charge than aluminum
options.explanation: Both have similar nuclear charge, but magnesium has a filled subshell which increases stability.

options.text: Aluminum has a higher nuclear charge than magnesium
options.explanation: Aluminum has a slightly higher nuclear charge, but this is not the primary reason for the ionization energy anomaly.

options.text: Magnesium has a completely filled s-subshell, whereas aluminum has an electron in the p-subshell
options.explanation: The filled s-subshell in magnesium makes it more stable, leading to higher ionization energy compared to aluminum.

options.text: The atomic size of magnesium is smaller than that of aluminum
options.explanation: Magnesium is actually smaller in atomic size than aluminum, but this is not the primary reason for the ionization energy anomaly.

questions.explanation: Magnesium (atomic number 12) has a completely filled 3s subshell (3s2), making it more stable. Aluminum (atomic number 13) has an electron in the 3p subshell, which is easier to remove, resulting in a lower ionization energy than expected.
questions.hint: Compare the electronic configurations of magnesium and aluminum to understand the difference in ionization energies.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements is expected to have the smallest atomic radius?

options.text: Lithium
options.explanation: Lithium is in Period 2 but has a larger atomic radius than fluorine.

options.text: Sodium
options.explanation: Sodium is in Period 3 and has a much larger atomic radius than fluorine.

options.text: Potassium
options.explanation: Potassium is in Period 4 and has the largest atomic radius among the given options.

options.text: Fluorine
options.explanation: Fluorine has the smallest atomic radius among the given options due to its high nuclear charge.

questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period from left to right. Among the given options, fluorine (F), in Period 2, has the smallest atomic radius because it has the highest nuclear charge in its period, pulling electrons closer.
questions.hint: Identify the element located furthest to the right in the periodic table among the given options.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the position of hydrogen in the Modern Periodic Table?

options.text: Hydrogen is placed in Group 1 because it has one electron
options.explanation: While hydrogen has one electron, its properties do not match Group 1 elements.

options.text: Hydrogen is placed in Group 17 because it can gain one electron
options.explanation: Hydrogen can gain an electron like Group 17 elements, but its properties do not match them consistently.

options.text: Hydrogen is placed separately as its properties are unique and do not fit into any group
options.explanation: Hydrogen is placed separately in the periodic table due to its unique properties.

options.text: Hydrogen is placed in Group 2 because it forms a positive ion
options.explanation: Hydrogen does not fit into Group 2 as it does not have properties similar to alkaline earth metals.

questions.explanation: Hydrogen is placed separately in the Modern Periodic Table because it does not fit neatly into any group. It can lose an electron to form H+ (like Group 1), gain an electron to form H- (like Group 17), or share electrons (like Group 14). Its properties are unique and do not match any group consistently.
questions.hint: Consider the unique properties of hydrogen and its inability to fit into any single group.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct according to the Modern Periodic Law?

options.text: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses.
options.explanation: This is incorrect. The Modern Periodic Law is based on atomic numbers, not atomic masses.

options.text: Properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
options.explanation: Correct. This is the correct statement of the Modern Periodic Law.

options.text: Properties of elements repeat every 9th element.
options.explanation: Incorrect. There is no such rule in the Modern Periodic Law.

options.text: Properties of elements are a function of their valency.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Valency is a result of electron configuration, not the basis of the Modern Periodic Law.

questions.explanation: The Modern Periodic Law states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
questions.hint: Recall the Modern Periodic Law definition.

questions.question: The atomic radii of the elements of the second period decrease from lithium to fluorine. Which of the following best explains this trend?

options.text: The nuclear charge increases and the electrons are added to the same shell.
options.explanation: Correct. Increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer, reducing atomic radius.

options.text: The number of electrons increases.
options.explanation: Incorrect. While the number of electrons increases, it is not the primary reason for the decrease in atomic radius.

options.text: The atomic mass increases.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Atomic mass does not directly influence atomic radius.

options.text: The number of neutrons increases.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Neutrons do not affect the atomic radius.

questions.explanation: As we move from lithium to fluorine in the second period, the nuclear charge increases due to the addition of protons, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus and reducing the atomic radius.
questions.hint: Consider the effect of increasing nuclear charge on the electrons.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The first ionization energy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen. Reason (R): Nitrogen has a half-filled p-orbital, which is more stable than the electronic configuration of oxygen.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct. Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect. The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Assertion A is true.

questions.explanation: Nitrogen has a half-filled p-orbital (1s² 2s² 2p³), which is more stable. Oxygen (1s² 2s² 2p⁴) has a paired electron in the p-orbital, which is easier to remove, resulting in lower ionization energy.
questions.hint: Consider the electronic configurations of nitrogen and oxygen.

questions.question: Consider the following elements: Na, Mg, Al, Si. Which of the following correctly represents the increasing order of their melting points?

options.text: Na < Mg < Al < Si
options.explanation: Correct. The order matches the increasing melting points of the elements.

options.text: Si < Al < Mg < Na
options.explanation: Incorrect. This is the reverse order of melting points.

options.text: Na < Si < Mg < Al
options.explanation: Incorrect. Silicon has a much higher melting point than magnesium and aluminum.

options.text: Mg < Na < Al < Si
options.explanation: Incorrect. Magnesium has a higher melting point than sodium.

questions.explanation: The melting points increase across the period from Na to Si due to the increasing strength of metallic bonds (Na) to covalent network bonds (Si). The correct order is Na (97.72°C) < Mg (650°C) < Al (660.3°C) < Si (1414°C).
questions.hint: Consider the type of bonding present in each element.
questions.subject: icse10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the decrease in reactivity of halogens down the group?

options.text: The atomic size decreases down the group.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Atomic size actually increases down the group.

options.text: The electronegativity decreases down the group.
options.explanation: Correct. Decreasing electronegativity leads to lower reactivity.

options.text: The ionization energy decreases down the group.
options.explanation: Incorrect. While ionization energy decreases, it is not the primary reason for the decrease in reactivity.

options.text: The nuclear charge increases down the group.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Nuclear charge increases, but atomic size increases more significantly, reducing electronegativity.

questions.explanation: The reactivity of halogens decreases down the group because the atomic size increases, leading to a decrease in electronegativity. Fluorine, being the smallest and most electronegative, is the most reactive.
questions.hint: Consider the trend in electronegativity down Group 17.
